ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended), Articles 19 and 23; Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as most recently amended), Articles 5-2, 5-3 and 7; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 5493, as amended); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 5777, as amended); Financial Services Commission regulations on customer identification and beneficial owner verification; and Korean FIU counter-terrorism financing directives implementing United Nations Security Council Resolutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Chusik Hoesa Company Registration Certificate and certified corporate registry extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (court with jurisdiction over the registered office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public; then either (a) Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member, or (b) MOFA authentication followed by Consular Legalization at the destination-state embassy or consulate in Seoul if the destination state is not an Apostille member. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean certificate of corporate existence and current registration status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office (court having jurisdiction over the registered office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public; then either (a) Hague Apostille by MOFA for Apostille Convention destination states, or (b) MOFA authentication plus Consular Legalization by the destination-country consulate in Seoul for non-Apostille destination states. Only one authentication path applies per destination; never sequential chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the overseas incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, notarized by a licensed Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean notarization of signatures and corporate seal attestation; then either (a) Hague Apostille by MOFA if the receiving jurisdiction is Apostille Convention member, or (b) MOFA authentication followed by Consular Legalization at the receiving state's diplomatic mission in Seoul for non-member jurisdictions. Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive routes and must not be applied one after the other.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and founding shareholders; certified copy issued by the Korean Registry Office after registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Korean notary of the approved articles and, where relevant, corporate seal; then either (a) Hague Apostille by MOFA for Apostille Convention destination states, or (b) MOFA authentication plus Consular Legalization at the destination-state consulate/embassy in Seoul for non-Apostille states. The chosen path depends exclusively on the destination state's membership status; both paths are never used for the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean commercial bank verifying company relationship and transactional conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed commercial bank maintaining or opening the corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank branch manager attestation under the bank's corporate seal; for foreign regulatory use, the letter must first be notarized, then either (a) Hague Apostille by MOFA if the destination jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, or (b) MOFA authentication followed by Consular Legalization at the destination jurisdiction's embassy or consulate in Seoul if it is not an Apostille member. Apostille and Consular Legalization are exclusive alternatives and must never be combined sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners must be screened against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Korean domestic sanctions and counter-terrorism designations issued under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information. Any positive PEP match triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds documentation, senior management approval and an elevated risk rating. Any sanctions hit is disqualifying, blocked, and must be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 24 hours. Continuous monitoring must cover adverse media, beneficial ownership changes and transaction pattern anomalies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS - Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (www.iros.go.kr) company name availability and registration system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean company names must be expressed in Hangul; a foreign-language name does not by itself create name exclusivity under the Commercial Act. The registry examines Hangul spelling, phonetic transliteration, and visual/verbal confusion with existing registered names. The four-tier statutory naming conventions for Korean companies are Chusik Hoesa (stock company), Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), Habmyeong Hoesa (unlimited partnership), and Hapja Hoesa (limited partnership), each requiring its statutory designation suffix. Foreign corporate names are transliterated into Hangul according to the standards of the National Institute of Korean Language, and English names may be used only as auxiliary trade names where permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must file a written objection with the supporting registry office within 14 days of notice, stating the statutory basis, the proposed Hangul name and evidence showing absence of confusion with prior registered names. If rejected again, the applicant may initiate a non-contentious case in the district court having jurisdiction for judicial review. The objection must attach the original rejection notice, the IROS search result and, if helpful, a Korean intellectual-property attorney's opinion on distinctiveness. A lapsed name reservation cannot be extended; a fresh reservation must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Commercial Act, the registered office must be a definite place capable of receiving official notices and identifying the company's central administration. A virtual office address may satisfy registration-only requirements if the service provider physically receives and forwards mail. However, for ISIC 5210 cross-dock/overseas warehouse order fulfillment, the National Tax Service (NTS) generally requires a physical place of business for VAT business registration, tax invoice issuance and customs inventory records. Korean banks also reject virtual-only addresses for corporate account opening because of Financial Services Commission AML CDD rules requiring physical substance verification. Therefore, a virtual office is acceptable only as an interim registered address; a physical commercial lease or warehouse operating site is effectively mandatory for NTS approval and bank onboarding.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for NTS, municipal tax, and customs inspections: company name signboard, lease or sublease agreement, utility bill, payroll and labor records, warehouse inventory movement records, cross-docking receipts, customs import/export declarations, VAT tax invoices, IT/warehouse equipment, CCTV, fire and safety certificates, and a designated on-site responsible manager. Quantified risk: municipal tax office on-site inspection probability is 25-40% in the first operating year for e-commerce logistics operators; customs inspection probability is 20-30% if bonded or duty-deferral inventory is declared; NTS VAT desk or field audit probability is 15-30% where sales are concentrated in overseas fulfillment. Use of a purely virtual office materially increases the risk of administrative de-registration or tax invoice cancellation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, particularly Articles 288 (Articles of Incorporation), 289 (Provisions to be included), 290 (Certification of Articles), 291 (Subscribers), 292 (Methods of Subscription), 295 (Payment of Subscription Price), 299 (Election of Directors and Statutory Auditors), 306 (Registration), 317 (Registration of Incorporation), 330 (Effective Date), together with Article 10 of the Korean Valuation Act and the Framework Agreement on Corporate Registration under the Court Organization Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporation Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the Company's registered head office address (Deung-gi-so), supervised by the Supreme Court Registration Bureau; online lodgment via the 'I-Registration' portal of the Supreme Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) together with Application for Corporation Registration (Beobin Deung-gi) and Report of Incorporation, plus the Certificate of Subscription and Payment Receipt.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa under the amended Korean Commercial Act. However, at the time of incorporation, at least 100 Korean won per issued share must be fully paid in, and subscription payments must be deposited into a blocked account at a Korean licensed financial institution in the name of the proposed company (or deposited as in-kind property with court-appointed inspection if required). The deposit remains frozen until the completion of incorporation registration; there is no separate escrow account requirement, but the blocked deposit fulfils the statutory paid-in capital protection rule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), a Chusik Hoesa incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, adopted unanimously by the initial directors at the first board meeting held on [Date] at [Place], following approval by the subscribers at the incorporation assembly. WHEREAS, the Company has been organized in the form of a Chusik Hoesa with limited liability; WHEREAS, the subscribers have executed a subscription agreement for the Company's ordinary shares; WHEREAS, the share subscription price has been tendered to the paying agency designated in the incorporation procedures; and WHEREAS, the directors and statutory auditor have been elected in accordance with Articles 299 and 302 of the Commercial Act. NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved and hereby ordered as follows: 1. Share Subscription Price and Paid-in Capital. The Board ratifies the issue and subscription of [number] ordinary shares at KRW [amount] per share, totaling KRW [paid-in capital]. The Board confirms that the full subscription price has been paid into the blocked deposit account at [Bank] under the Company's name, and directs the Representative Director to maintain this blocked balance until the registration of incorporation is completed. Capital and share premium, if any, shall be recorded in accordance with Article 290 of the Commercial Act. 2. Bank Accounts and Payment Rails. The Board approves the opening of corporate settlement and foreign-currency accounts with [Bank] and authorizes the Representative Director to execute all account documents. The Board approves the use of the Company's target payment rails, including local ACH, Airwallex, and international wire transfers, for the settlement of cross-docking and overseas 3PL services. 3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [Full address], Republic of Korea. All statutory registers, share ledgers, and accounting books shall be kept at the registered office or at the head office, and the Representative Director is directed to file the registration of the office address with the competent court registration division. 4. Statutory Officers. The Board appoints [Director A] as Representative Director, [Director B] as Director, and [Auditor] as Statutory Auditor, each to hold office until the next ordinary general meeting and until successors are appointed. The Board also confirms that the Company shall appoint an external auditor if required by Article 4 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. 5. Corporate Governance. The Board directs the officers to prepare the Company's corporate seals, issue share certificates, and register the incorporation with the competent district court within two weeks after the resolution. The Board further directs the Representative Director to obtain the business registration certificate from the competent tax office and to procure all relevant warehouse facility operating permits. This resolution is effective immediately. All previous resolutions are superseded. Dated and signed by the Board of Directors this [date]. /s/ [Director A] / /s/ [Director B]

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: Hometax Service (www.hometax.go.kr). Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS, www.unipass.customs.go.kr) for export declarations and customs registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act through the Supreme Court Registration Office; the court registry transmits incorporation notice to the competent NTS district tax office for automatic business registration. 2) For a foreign non-resident entity without a domestic place of business, appoint a statutory domestic tax representative and file the foreign corporation business registration application with the district tax office at the domestic tax manager's location, attaching the home-country certificate of incorporation, certificate of registration or equivalent, board resolution appointing the tax manager, and power of attorney. 3) NTS through Hometax assigns a ten-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) that serves as the unified Tax Identification Number / VAT ID for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding obligations, customs clearance, and electronic tax invoice issuance. 4) Register separately with Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS to obtain an exporter code; this code is required for filing export declarations on physical export cross-dock and overseas fulfillment flows. 5) Maintain the original Business Registration Certificate, report changes within the statutory window, and activate the electronic tax invoice issuance certificate in Hometax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch entity classification election applicable to a Chusik Hoesa; a resident stock corporation is a taxable legal person by statute. No VAT grouping election is available for this single-entity structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory turnover threshold for this corporation; VAT registration is mandatory within 20 days of business commencement. Simplified taxpayer treatment with the KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover threshold is available only to individuals, not to a Chusik Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) are mandatory under the Korean VAT Act and must be issued and transmitted through the NTS Hometax electronic tax invoice network. Submission is made via Hometax web portal, EDI, or the Hometax application using an accredited digital certificate. Accepted e-tax invoices receive an NTS reference number; Korea does not operate a private third-party real-time invoice clearance model or physical fiscal stamp. Anti-fraud integrity rests on the taxpayer's certified digital signature, NTS transmission acknowledgment, and the unique e-tax invoice numbering scheme.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (a) physical goods exported from Korea where the export declaration has been filed and accepted under the Customs Act, title and risk pass to an overseas buyer, and the goods are removed from Korea; (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient for use outside Korea, including qualifying logistics, warehousing, or cross-dock fulfillment services directly connected to exported goods, provided the services are not treated as domestic taxable supplies; and (c) export proceeds are received in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The taxpayer must report the zero-rated export supplies in the periodic VAT return and retain full documentary evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration acceptance through UNI-PASS)
Bill of Lading (master and house, as applicable)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Sale Confirmation (FESC) issued by the Korean dealing bank
Proof of export transportation and overseas warehouse delivery (Cargo Tracking, Delivery Confirmation, and away-from-port records)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit zero-rated exports. If the export evidence bundle is incomplete, export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days (unless extension is approved), or the zero-rating is found to be fraudulent or overstated, the tax office will reverse the zero-rating and assess unpaid VAT at 10% on the supply value, plus negligent filing penalty tax and aggravated fraudulent penalty tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Fraudulent cases may attract criminal referral, monetary fines, and retrospective reassessment. The standard statutory assessment period is five years, extended to ten years for evasion or fraudulent return.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting in concert with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Federation of Banks' Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a formally liberalized yet carefully supervised two-tier foreign exchange regime. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, current account transactions -- including dividend remittances, service fees, and ordinary trade settlements -- are generally free and may be processed through licensed foreign exchange banks with only a post-transaction reporting obligation to FEIS. Capital account transactions, such as equity injections, loans, and scriptural investments, require prior or simultaneous notification for statistical balance of payments purposes, but no ex ante authorization is needed for standard foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA). The Korean won (KRW) is considered convertible for current account purposes, but the market remains intervened by the BOK under a floating exchange rate system. For the Chusik Hoesa, profit remittance hurdles are non-trivial: the entity must first present documentation proving prior tax withholding, completed foreign exchange bank due diligence, and a completed transaction report through FEIS for amounts above KRW 500 million or USD equivalent. Surplus capital repatriation is likewise permitted under FIPA after a certified capital verification by paid-in capital and actual investment confirmation. In practice, the convertibility is robust for bona fide operating entities, but the friction point is documentary completeness; every cross-border transfer must be supported by the underlying contract, invoice, or tax certificate, and the bank's compliance unit will subject the transfer to a release check against the economic substance of the transaction. There is no mandatory conversion of export proceeds into KRW, but exporters must report the collection within the statutory timeline and may hold the funds in a foreign currency account. Overall, the regime is business-friendly but demands rigorous real-time reporting and conservative bank audit trails, making an unbanked fintech route impossible for onshore KRW settlement.

stage_4.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 12-2 and Article 39 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, an exporter must collect export proceeds in foreign currency within 2 years from the date of export declaration (for goods) or from the date of service performance (for services). There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; proceeds may be retained in a foreign currency account at a licensed foreign exchange bank or converted to KRW at the prevailing market rate. However, the receipt must be reported through FEIS within 6 business days after collection. For export declarations valued over USD 50,000, the customs export declaration itself constitutes the collection report, and no separate surrender requirement applies. The 2-year period can be extended once for a further year upon application to the foreign exchange bank for justified commercial reasons.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders and approval of annual financial statements, including minutes and statutory register verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate body; no external filing to a government registry, but statutory registers must be available for shareholder, creditor and court inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the ordinary general meeting without justifiable grounds are subject to administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000; financial statements approved late or without audit may be invalid for dividend distribution; repeated non-compliance may lead to court-administered dissolution under Commercial Act Article 176.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with annual statutory financial statements and supporting tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Korea, via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, due by March 31 of the immediately following calendar year; a one-month extension is available only with NTS approval or as provided for companies with foreign branches or qualified tax-agent engagement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate tax liability; under-reporting triggers 10% of the omitted tax (30% for intentional concealment); overdue amounts accrue late-payment interest of 0.025% per day; persistent non-compliance can lead to asset seizure, cancellation of business registration and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surcharge return on corporate income tax payable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office where the head office is located (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government Tax Division)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the corporate income tax return, generally March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end, subject to any extended corporate tax deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid local income tax surcharge; under-reporting penalty of 10% or 30% depending on intent; daily late-payment interest of 0.025% per day; local tax enforcement including compulsory collection and seizure of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external audit report and audited financial statements, filed with the financial regulator and presented to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; copies filed with the National Tax Service and presented at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a non-listed company subject to mandatory audit with a December 31 fiscal year-end, completion and submission of the audit report is required by March 31; for listed public-interest companies, earlier periodic disclosure deadlines may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor is subject to FSC corrective orders and administrative fines; late filing of the audit report can result in fines for negligence up to KRW 30,000,000; statutory financial statements without an auditor's report cannot lawfully support dividend declarations and can invalidate shareholder approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested company annual status report and 30-day change report, applicable if foreign shareholding triggers the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) on behalf of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual foreign-investment status report for the preceding calendar year due by February 28 (or February 29 in a leap year); any change in registered foreign-investment facts, including share transfers or capital issuance, must be reported within 30 calendar days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the 30-day window or the annual deadline may result in administrative fines under FIPA, loss of foreign-investment tax protections or incentives, and disqualification of the entity from designated foreign-invested status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory corporate records, registers, and minute book review and maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; records kept at the head office or registered domestic place of business; inspection rights vest in shareholders, creditors and court-appointed inspectors; tax courts may require production
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous event-driven maintenance: update the shareholders' register immediately after each share transfer or pledge; minute books for any shareholders' or board meeting must be completed and available for inspection within 2 weeks after the meeting; annual records reconciliation to be completed before the March 31 corporate tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Refusal to allow inspection or maintenance of inaccurate registers exposes directors to administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000 and personal joint and several liability; unrecorded share transfers are ineffective against the company; egregious non-maintenance can result in court-ordered strike-off where the company ceases to maintain a real, registrable presence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (as amended, Act No. 15677), a Korean Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily required to appoint an independent certified CPA auditor if, as of the immediately preceding fiscal year-end, its balance-sheet total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9.0 million). The audit obligation also applies without regard to asset size if the company is: (i) a listed issuer on KOSPI/KOSDAQ; (ii) a financial institution, financial holding company or otherwise separately regulated under financial services law; (iii) designated as a public-interest company by the Financial Services Commission (FSC); or (iv) required to present consolidated financial statements under the External Audit Act. There is no standalone turnover-only or headcount-only statutory audit trigger for ordinary unlisted private companies; turnover and headcount are relevant only where the FSC, exercising designation power, classifies the company as subject to external audit based on public-interest criteria. A company below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold, and not otherwise designated, is not statutorily required to undergo an independent audit, unless the company voluntarily opts for an audit under the Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public-interest companies and listed companies must apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS). Non-listed companies subject to external audit may apply either K-IFRS or the Korean General Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP or SME Accounting Standards) approved by the Korea Accounting Institute and the FSC. For corporate income tax filing, taxable income must be computed under the Corporation Tax Act and reconciled to the financial statements prepared under the applicable accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently maintain a general annual beneficial-ownership declaration regime for ordinary private stock corporations. The principal statutory ownership record is the shareholders' registry (Register of Members) kept under the Commercial Act; a share transfer is effective against the company only upon entry of the transferee into that register. Bearer shares are prohibited for Chusik Hoesa. For a company registered as a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the foreign investor must file an annual foreign-investment status return with KOTRA/MOTIE by the statutory annual deadline and must report any change in registered facts, including shareholding transfers or changes in ownership ratio, to KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 calendar days from the occurrence of the change. For purely domestic share transfers, no stand-alone 30-day government filing is required; but the company must promptly update the shareholders' register and reflect the transfer in any corporate tax reporting. An internal annual confirmation exercise is recommended to reconcile actual shareholders, officers, charges and registered share certificates with the statutory registers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Auditors (roster of officers)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (if any security interest or encumbrance over shares or assets exists)
Minute Book of Shareholders' General Meetings and Board of Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per annum for a commercial registered address, corporate secretarial, or in-house compliance service in Seoul/Busan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per annum for a non-listed ISIC 5210 cross-dock/overseas warehouse 3PL company if a statutory audit is mandatory; USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 per annum for a voluntary review or agreed-upon procedures engagement where no statutory audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive corporate income tax of 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% over KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% over KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion and 24% over KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income tax surtax on the corporate income tax payable (aggregate statutory range 9.9%-26.4%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Special Tax Treatment Control Act incentives include: 100% corporate income tax holidays for five years followed by a 50% reduction for two years for qualifying high-tech foreign-invested businesses in Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones; R&D expense tax credits, employment and venture business tax reductions; no patent box regime but IP-related R&D incentives may reduce the effective rate for qualified domestic or cross-border 3PL technology operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 21-1) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr) together with the statutory financial statements, tax adjustment schedules and related-party transaction disclosures.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; interim advance prepayments are made twice per year for corporations with revenue exceeding KRW 50 billion, but the final corporate tax return is filed annually.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity the deadline is March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension is generally available when audited financial statements are attached, and further extension up to six months for consolidated or specified large taxpayers is possible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identification and Business Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Korean business registration number, corporate name, head office, representative director, domicile tax office, fiscal year begin and end dates, industry code ISIC 5210 / NAICS 493110 and filing status (ordinary, audited, amended or non-reportable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Korean Chusik Hoesa, identify the entity as a domestic resident corporation and do not use branch-payment or foreign-corporation schedules. Attach the shareholder register and ownership schedule showing ultimate non-resident beneficial owners so that DTA relief can be evaluated before distribution; a foreign nominee shareholder without substance should be treated as a Korean resident controlling party for substance purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Income Statement and Gross Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total sales, cost of goods sold, gross profit, SG&A expenses, operating income, non-operating income and non-operating expenses derived from the Korean statutory income statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all revenue from cross-docking, overseas order fulfillment, warehouse storage, picking, packing, shipping, and logistics services. For foreign customers, Korea-source income attributable to the Korean warehouse PE must be recognized; the mere routing of orders through a foreign e-commerce front-end does not allow exclusion of the fulfillment revenue from the Korean tax return. Reconcile revenue with customs or overseas warehouse confirmations if audited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Convert financial income to taxable income by adding back non-deductible expenses such as excess entertainment, fines, non-deductible reserves, excess depreciation and unjustified reserves, and by deducting tax-exempt income and permitted reserve additions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, administrative service fees, royalties and interest paid to foreign related parties must be supported by an arm's length arrangement and a functional analysis. If the NTS finds the payment lacks benefit or economic substance, the expense is disallowed and added to taxable income under Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs; attach TP adjustment schedules with the selected methodology and comparable analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Loss Carryforward and Taxable Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carry the adjusted taxable income from Box 3 and subtract deductible loss carryforwards, untaxed reserves and tax-exempt income to arrive at the taxable base for the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Korean legal entity's own cumulative losses may be deducted within the statutory carryforward period; losses generated by a foreign related party, a disregarded offshore warehouse, or a flow-through edge entity cannot be transferred into the Korean return. If a foreign merger or spin-off occurred, preserve the legal-continuity documentation required by the NTS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive CIT rate to the taxable base, compute the tentative tax, deduct non-resident/foreign tax credits, investment, employment and R&D credits, then compute 10% local income tax surtax on the final corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean 3PL corporation with foreign branches or overseas warehouses must attach Foreign Tax Credit schedules for foreign income taxes actually paid and show the source and category of income. The NTS will deny the credit if the foreign entity lacks substance or if the income is recharacterized as a Korean-source service profit; treaty tie-breaker rules should be checked before claiming the credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Dividend Distribution and Withholding Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare dividends paid or distributable to shareholders, the amount per class of shares, and the withholding tax payable on each distribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before remitting an outbound dividend, the Korean corporation must withhold 22% aggregate (20% CIT withholding plus 2% local income tax). If the foreign recipient provides a Tax Residency Certificate and an approved DTA relief form, the reduced treaty rate is applied at remittance; otherwise, the statutory rate is remitted and refund may be claimed. Constructive dividends arising from excessive related-party payments must also be reported and withheld here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, by counterparty, type, amount and transfer pricing method, and indicate whether a Local File or Master File is maintained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the aggregate foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion, the Local File must be available and the Master File must be submitted when the consolidated revenue threshold is met; a transaction with a non-resident agent, sister company or ultimate beneficial owner must be disclosed even if the counterparty is located in a treaty jurisdiction. Incomplete disclosure is assessed independently of the income tax deficiency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual return triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid tax amount; fraudulent or dishonest filing triggers an additional tax equal to 40%. Unpaid taxes accrue a daily late-payment additional tax of 0.022% from the due date until payment. Failure to submit transfer pricing documentation may trigger a separate penalty under Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and intentional evasion exceeding substantial thresholds exposes the company and directors to imprisonment and fines under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding imposed on outbound dividends (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax); treaty rates generally range from 0% to 15%, with 10% being common for direct qualified shareholdings of 25% or more, provided the beneficial owner condition is satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA at source, the paying Korean company must obtain, before payment, the foreign shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence jurisdiction for the relevant year, a completed Korean Application for Exemption/Reduction of Korean Withholding Tax under the applicable tax treaty, a Beneficial Ownership Declaration signed by the ultimate shareholder, and supporting substance evidence such as annual report, employee headcount and financial statements if requested by the NTS. The application must be submitted to the NTS together with the withholding declaration or before the remittance date; after tax was withheld at the statutory rate, a refund or rectification claim may be filed with the TRC and transaction contracts within the general five-year claim period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalties paid to nonresidents are subject to 22% aggregate statutory withholding (20% plus 2% local income tax). Treaty rates vary by jurisdiction: interest is often reduced to 10%-15% and royalties to 5%-15%, but royalties for the use of intangibles paid to a related foreign entity without actual ownership, development, maintenance, enhancement, protection and exploitation (DEMPE) functions may be disallowed as deductible expense and still be taxed at the statutory WHT rate on the deemed distribution.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50,000,000,000 (KRW 50 billion) in annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers the Local File requirement; the Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue is at least KRW 100 billion and the Korean entity's foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion. Smaller transactions below KRW 100 million per related counterparty may qualify for simplified documentation, but the overall documentation obligation remains screened by the NTS.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulation statute of the UAE model, but the NTS applies the substance-over-form principle under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 and International Tax Coordination Law. The Korean warehouse entity must perform Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Korea: physical warehouse management, cross-docking operations, inventory and order processing, freight coordination, credit and collection risk, and strategic logistics decisions through employees, premises and board meetings
